heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
sections.text: As AI tools increasingly influence instruction, assessment, and administration, FCCPS must ensure that their use advances equity, access, and student well-being. Equity considerations should be embedded from the start of all AI-related decisions, not added after tools or practices are already in place. The following policy recommendations outline priority considerations for those with authority over district-level equity and technology policy.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text:
Make Equity a Foundational Requirement
Affirm that equity, accessibility, and disability accommodations are core criteria for all AI-related decisions—from procurement through classroom and administrative use. Students are a protected and vulnerable population requiring heightened safeguards.

sections.text: Recommendation: Adopt a clear policy statement affirming that equity, accessibility, and disability accommodations are core criteria for all AI-related decisions—from procurement through classroom practice and administrative use.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text: Our current working policy statement surrounding equity in community:

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text: FCCPS will evaluate AI tools and AI usage for equity and accessibility from the procurement stage to the classroom, including administrative uses. FCCPS will monitor and evaluate AI usage in terms of equity and access, and collect data on reported bias incidences. Monitoring and evaluation should be incorporated into relevant existing school structures. The committee must include, but is not limited to, School Technology Professionals, Special Education and English Language Learner coordinators.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text: Topics related to equity will be included as part of AI Literacy for students and staff. This will include understanding how models are trained and how to identify algorithmic bias.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text:
Adopt Guiding Principles With Structured Review
Pair district-level AI Equity & Access Guiding Principles with a proportionate equity review process for AI policies, tools, and workflows. Guiding principles articulate intent; structured review ensures consistent application without overburdening staff.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text: We initially set up a equity and accessibility checklist (See WS-EQA-1) however, felt that while a checklist was important, we did not have the proper resources from the district to determine how useful or unwieldy it could be. Please refer to WS-EQA-1 as a starting point should a checklist be desirable.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text: Our working guiding principle: How can we ensure that our approach to AI sufficiently continues to uphold the standards and values on learning that align with the IB program, and that AI is used in the service of those goals, including equity?

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text:
Prohibit High-Stakes Decisions Based Solely on AI Outputs
Disallow disciplinary, academic integrity, or profiling decisions based only on AI detection tools or automated risk indicators. Require human judgment, contextual evidence, and equitable dispute processes.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Key Policy Recommendations
sections.text:
Recognize AI Literacy as an Equity Issue
Commit to equitable AI literacy for students and staff that addresses AI limitations, bias, and responsible use—without assuming advanced technical expertise or creating unfunded expectations.

Track a limited number of high-value equity indicators (e.g., access barriers, accommodation conflicts, integrity disputes, bias reports) using existing structures where possible, and use findings to revisit policy when risks emerge.

heading_path: Equity and Accessibility in AI Use Across FCCPS Community
Closing Note
sections.text: Equitable AI policy is not about maximizing AI use, but about deciding when, how, and whether AI should be used at all. By centering equity early, FCCPS can reduce unintended harm, support educators, and uphold its values while responsibly navigating rapid technological change.
